{{Short description|Canadian medical researcher (1925–2025)}}
'''Marion Jean Lewis''' {{postnominals|OC|OM|FRSC}} (September 21, 1925 – October 18, 2025) was a Canadian medical researcher, known for her work on the [[Rh factor]]<ref name=Fonds/><ref name=RhLab/> and on the [[Duffy antigen system]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Chown, Bruce|author2=Lewis, Marion Lewis|author3=Kaita, Hiroko|title=The Duffy blood group system in Caucasians: evidence for a new allele|journal=American Journal of Human Genetics|volume=17|issue=5|year=1965|pages=384–389|pmc=1932660|pmid=14334737}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Lewis graduated from [[Winnipeg]]'s [[Gordon Bell High School]] in 1943. She was trained as a medical technician at [[Winnipeg General Hospital]]. In 1944, the pediatric pathologist [[Bruce Chown]], assisted by Lewis, opened the Rh Laboratory in Winnipeg to study and eradicate [[Rh disease]].<ref name="RhLab">{{cite web|title=Winnipeg Rh Laboratory|website=University of Manitoba Libraries|url=http://medheritage.lib.umanitoba.ca/?page_id=73proxycheck.lib.umanitoba.ca/libraries/units/archives/collections/rad/lewis_mj.html}}</ref><ref name="Fonds">{{cite web|title=Dr. Marion Lewis|website=University of Manitoba Libraries|url=https://umanitoba.ca/libraries/units/archives/collections/complete_holdings/ead/html/M.Lewis2.shtml|access-date=2019-06-06|archive-date=2016-03-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330065945/http://umanitoba.ca/libraries/units/archives/collections/complete_holdings/ead/html/M.Lewis2.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> Their research led to effective treatments and a vaccine that prevents Rh disease.<ref name="Herstory">{{cite book|title=Herstory 2009: The Canadian Women's Calendar|date=July 2008 |page=102|publisher=Coteau Books |isbn=9781550503890 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fyQaF0MAOc0C&pg=PA102}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Bowman, J. M.|authorlink=John Maxwell Bowman|author2=Chown, B.|author3=Lewis, M.|author4=Pollock, J. M.|year=1978|title=Rh isoimmunization during pregnancy: antenatal prophylaxis|journal=Canadian Medical Association Journal|volume=118|issue=6|pages=623–627|pmid=77714 |pmc=1818025}}</ref>

In 1950–51, Lewis spent four months at an Italian university studying the Italian language and culture. She then spent another three months studying in London under world-renowned ‘blood groupers’ [[Robert Russell Race|Robert Race]] and [[Ruth Sanger]]. In 1951, she returned to Winnipeg and the Rh lab.<ref name="Fonds" /> From 1952 and 1960, Chown and Lewis made annual trips, visiting Canadian tribal groups, including the [[Blackfoot]] and [[Cree]], to test their blood for Rh factors. They also tested [[Inuit]] at [[Kugluktuk]] and [[Southampton Island]] and [[Hutterites]] in Manitoba.<ref name="Fonds" />

While Chown retired in 1977, Lewis continued on in the field of blood group gene mapping and eventually branched out into the field of genetics. She and her colleagues at the Rh Laboratory, including Hiroko Kaita, became internationally renowned for their work.<ref name="Fonds" />

In the Department of Pediatrics at the [[University of Manitoba]]'s the Faculty of Medicine, Lewis was an assistant professor from 1973 to 1977, an associate professor from 1977 to 1984, and a full professor from 1984 to 1996, when she retired as professor emerita.<ref name="Fonds" /> She was the author or co-author of more than 140 articles.<ref name="Herstory" />

On 27 June 2019, Lewis was appointed an Officer to the [[Order of Canada]] for her contributions to the prevention and treatment of Rh disease.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gg.ca/en/media/news/2019/governor-general-announces-83-new-appointments-order-canada|title=Governor General Announces 83 New Appointments to the Order of Canada|last=General|first=Office of the Secretary to the Governor|date=2019-06-20|website=The Governor General of Canada|access-date=2019-06-27|archive-date=2019-06-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190628034534/https://www.gg.ca/en/media/news/2019/governor-general-announces-83-new-appointments-order-canada|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-2019-order-of-canada-appointees-have-made-their-mark-on-all-aspects-of/|title=2019 Order of Canada appointees have made their mark on all aspects of Canadian society|access-date=2019-06-27}}</ref> In 2020, Lewis was appointed a member of the [[Order of Manitoba]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manitobalg.ca/outstanding-manitobans-chosen-to-receive-the-order-of-manitoba-3/|title=Outstanding Manitobans chosen to receive the Order of Manitoba|publisher=Government of Manitoba|date=September 10, 2020}}</ref>

Lewis died in Winnipeg on October 18, 2025, at the age of 100.<ref>{{cite web |title=Marion Lewis |url=https://www.echovita.com/ca/obituaries/mb/winnipeg/marion-lewis-20529620 |website=Echovita |access-date=8 November 2025}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
* 1971 – [[Karl Landsteiner Memorial Award]] of the [[American Association of Blood Banks]] (AABB)
* 1986 – honorary D.Sc. from the University of Winnipeg
* 1993 – election as a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]]
* 1996 – Emily Cooley Memorial Award of the AABB
* 2019 – Officer of the [[Order of Canada]]
* 2020 – Member of the [[Order of Manitoba]]
